gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-lao: Bevellier looks cut from flat stencil stock, every stroke the same gauge and every glyph tucked tight to its neighbor. Noto Sans Lao follows with an oversized x-height and open mouths, so a long passage feels easy to settle into.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Bevellier sets its crossbars as heavy as its stems, giving the heading a flat, stencil-cut graze of confidence. Noto Sans Lao Looped keeps words in solid blocks.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Noto Sans Lepcha has a lowercase with the stature of cast iron capitals, and its curves stay wide open. Noto Sans Lepcha is the sturdy half here, while Bevellier supplies a graceful, constant-width outline you could trace with a finger.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu reads tall-bodied and gaping in its curves, a plain sans that leaves plenty of room inside each letter. Bevellier does wire-fine display drama; Noto Sans Limbu does the plain talking.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Bevellier draws like toothpaste squeezed in one steady line. Beneath it, Noto Sans Lisu keeps tiny gaps between ascender tops and the x-height line and opens its s wide, so the sans calms down what the heading stirs up.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Noto Sans Lydian keeps its capitals barely taller than the lowercase, with openings as wide as a sprung paper clip. Under Bevellier's bent-wire strokes, a long passage in it would move along gently and without fuss.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Flat ribbons, tightly spaced, all graceful. Bevellier shines as display, each glyph a ribbon of constant width, while Noto Sans Mahajani handles the reading with tall lowercase and a funnel-wide throat in the e.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Stencil-flat and sleek, Bevellier makes heavy bowls and stems match. And Noto Sans Malayalam rewards a generous size, since its dominant middle zone and open s bends have room to breathe.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Bevellier holds its diagonals as heavy as its verticals. It makes the display statement, and Noto Sans Mandaic, with lowercase rising close to the capitals and loose, curvy letters, does the quiet sans-serif work of carrying text.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Bevellier bends like tubing of one gauge, graceful and flat, and that is what it does best up top. Noto Sans Marchen does its own job below, with proud, almost capital-sized small letters and curves that end in clear daylight.
